title: HR Diagram: Axes and Layout
welcome_lead: Understand the unusual axes — and where each star lives.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: HR diagram axes, B-V index and log luminosity.
final_note: Once you can read the axes, the diagram tells its own story.

concepts.def: Colour index — blue minus visual magnitude.
Temperature of a blackbody of equal luminosity.
Energy radiated per second in watts or solar units.
Scale spaced by powers — used on the L axis.
x-axis runs from hot left to cool right.

walkthroughs.body_html: Temperature is on the x-axis and runs from hot on the left to cool on the right — the reverse of normal. The B-V index can replace temperature: bigger B-V means cooler and redder.
Luminosity is on the y-axis, plotted on a log scale from 10^-4 to 10^6 solar luminosities — six orders of magnitude. Absolute magnitude is sometimes used instead (smaller is brighter).
Plotting many stars shows the main sequence, giant branches and white dwarfs jump out as distinct regions. Cluster HR diagrams reveal ages because the main-sequence turnoff moves down with time.
